diagnosis.root_cause: The health-check alarm incorrectly reports all eight PONs as failed. The OLT, PON ports, subscriber ONU, and peer ONUs are operational; the alarm is stale or generated by a faulty health-check/probe condition.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, its OID subtree responds, and its uptime is approximately 58 days.
Current OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal at 24%, 18%, and 42C.
The subscriber ONU is online, authenticated, completes exchange, and has current readings of RX -19.71 dBm and TX 2.42 dBm, both healthy.
The subscriber's seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable, distance remains constant at 124, and TX bias remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.
All seven observed peers on EPON0/5 are online and responding, with healthy optical levels; the live PON probe confirms every sampled ONU is online.
The OLT has 207 of 214 ONUs online, which is consistent with the normal background offline rate and not an OLT-wide outage.
The customer VLAN is present and correct at VLAN 1035.
Router heartbeat and resource state are normal, and RADIUS records match CRM with normal session frequency and duration.
Therefore the reported 8/8 PON failure conflicts with live device and service evidence and is a false critical health-check result.

remediation.action: Suppress and clear the false alarm after verification, investigate the health-check logic and data source for TK_AF-OLT_KV03, and reconcile the alarm timestamp with current SNMP/PON results. No customer, ONU, fibre, router, VLAN, or RADIUS intervention is required.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
